tasks.title: First variable
tasks.statement:
Declare two variables: name with the value "Anya" and age with the value 30. Print them separated by a space: «Anya 30».

Expected output:
«Anya 30»
tasks.hint: let name = "Anya"; let age = 30; then println!("{} {}", name, age);

tasks.title: Sum and difference
tasks.statement:
Declare a = 17 and b = 5. Print two lines: «Sum: …» and «Difference: …», substituting the computed values.

Expected output:
«Sum: 22
Difference: 12»
tasks.hint: The expressions a + b and a - b can be passed straight to println!.

tasks.title: A counter with mut
tasks.statement:
Declare a mutable counter count = 0. Increase it by 1 three times (count = count + 1), and after each step print its value: 1, 2, 3 — one per line.

Expected output:
1
2
3
tasks.hint: let mut count = 0; then three times: count = count + 1; and println!.

tasks.title: Compound assignments
tasks.statement:
Start with n = 10 (mut). Perform in order n += 5, n -= 3, n *= 2, n /= 4, n %= 4, and print n after each operation: five lines.

Expected output:
15
12
24
6
2
tasks.hint: After each operation — println!("{}", n); the results: 15, 12, 24, 6, 2.

tasks.title: Fix it: cannot assign twice
tasks.statement:
The program does not build: the variable is immutable, and it is assigned a second time. Fix the declaration so that the program prints 5 and then 10.

Expected output:
5
10
tasks.hint: Add the word mut: let mut x = 5;

tasks.title: Fix it: an accumulator without mut
tasks.statement:
The program should print the total 12, but total is declared immutable. Fix it.

Expected output:
12
tasks.hint: An accumulator is always mutable: let mut total = 0;

tasks.title: Shadowing step by step
tasks.statement:
Declare x = 5, then shadow it: x = x + 1, then x = x * 2. Print x after each declaration: 5, 6, 12.

Expected output:
5
6
12
tasks.hint: Each time write a new let x = …; it is not a change but a new variable.

tasks.title: Shadowing with a new type
tasks.statement:
Declare data = "12345" (a string). Shadow it with the string length data.len(). Print «Length: 5».

Expected output:
«Length: 5»
tasks.hint: let data = data.len(); — the variable is now a number, not a string.

tasks.title: Fix it: mut cannot change the type
tasks.statement:
The program wants to turn a string into its length under the same name, but this is impossible through assignment (mismatched types). Fix it with shadowing. The result: «Length: 6».

Expected output:
«Length: 6»
tasks.hint: Instead of s = … write a new let s = …; s.len() is the length of the string in bytes (for ASCII it equals the number of characters).

tasks.title: Time constants
tasks.statement:
Declare the constants SECONDS_PER_MINUTE: u32 = 60 and MINUTES_PER_HOUR: u32 = 60. Compute and print how many seconds there are in 3 hours: «10800».

Expected output:
10800
tasks.hint: Constants are declared outside fn main — above it; the type is required: const NAME: u32 = 60;

tasks.title: Circumference
tasks.statement:
Declare the constant PI: f64 = 3.14159. The radius is r = 10.0. Print the circumference 2·PI·r with two decimal places: «62.83».

Expected output:
62.83

tasks.title: Blocks and shadowing
tasks.statement:
Declare x = 1. In a nested block { … } shadow x with the value 100 and print it (100). After the block print x again (1).

Expected output:
100
1
tasks.hint: The inner x lives until the closing brace of the block; after the block the old variable is visible.

tasks.title: A block as an expression
tasks.statement:
A block { … } is also an expression: its value is its last line without a semicolon. Declare y = { let x = 3; x * x + 1 }; and print y (10).

Expected output:
10
tasks.hint: The last expression in a block has no semicolon: it becomes the value of the block.

tasks.title: Explicit types
tasks.statement:
Declare three variables with explicit types: a: i64 = 3_000_000_000, b: u8 = 255, c: f32 = 1.5. Print them one per line.

Expected output:
3000000000
255
1.5
tasks.hint: The type is written after a colon; underscores inside a number are just for readability.

tasks.title: Number literal forms
tasks.statement:
Print on one line separated by spaces the values of the literals: 1_000_000, 0xff, 0b1010, 0o17 (the decimal values will be: 1000000 255 10 15).

Expected output:
1000000 255 10 15
tasks.hint: 0x is a hexadecimal, 0b a binary, 0o an octal literal.

tasks.title: Swap through a third variable
tasks.statement:
a = 3, b = 8 (mut). Swap the values using a temporary variable tmp. Print «a=8 b=3» after the swap.

Expected output:
a=8 b=3
tasks.hint: tmp = a; a = b; b = tmp; — the order matters.

tasks.title: Swap through a tuple
tasks.statement:
The same as in the previous task, but without a temporary variable: (a, b) = (b, a);. a = 3, b = 8; print «a=8 b=3».

Expected output:
a=8 b=3
tasks.hint: On the right the tuple (b, a) is built first, then it is unpacked into a and b.

tasks.title: Unpacking a tuple
tasks.statement:
Unpack the tuple (1, 2.5, "three") into variables x, y, z with a single let. Print «1 2.5 three».

Expected output:
«1 2.5 three»
tasks.hint: let (x, y, z) = (…); — three variables at once.

tasks.title: Assign later
tasks.statement:
Declare let grade; without a value. If score (= 85) is not less than 60, assign «passed», otherwise «not passed». Print «Grade: passed».

Expected output:
«Grade: passed»
tasks.hint: if condition { … } else { … } — in Rust the condition has no parentheses; in each branch grade is assigned exactly once.

tasks.title: Rectangle
tasks.statement:
width = 12, height = 5. Print two lines: «Area: 60» and «Perimeter: 34».

Expected output:
«Area: 60
Perimeter: 34»
tasks.hint: The area is width * height, the perimeter is 2 * (width + height).

tasks.title: Account balance
tasks.statement:
balance = 1000 (mut). Deposit 250, withdraw 400, deposit 75. After each operation print the balance: 1250, 850, 925.

Expected output:
1250
850
925
tasks.hint: balance += 250; balance -= 400; balance += 75; and println! after each line.

tasks.title: Celsius → Fahrenheit by shadowing
tasks.statement:
temp = 36.6 (degrees Celsius). Shadow it with the value in Fahrenheit (× 9 / 5 + 32) and print it with one decimal place: «97.9».

Expected output:
97.9
tasks.hint: Write fractional numbers with a dot: 9.0, 5.0, 32.0.

tasks.title: Average of three numbers
tasks.statement:
a = 4, b = 7, c = 10 (integers). Print the arithmetic mean with three decimal places: «7.000». Convert the sum to a floating-point number with as f64.

Expected output:
7.000
tasks.hint: An integer is converted to a float explicitly: sum as f64.

tasks.title: A block result and shadowing
tasks.statement:
Declare n = 10. In a block shadow n = n * 2 + 1 and return the value from the block into the variable r. Print «r=21 n=10».

Expected output:
r=21 n=10
tasks.hint: The block returns its last expression (n without a semicolon); the outer n does not change.

tasks.title: A manual countdown
tasks.statement:
n = 3 (mut). Print n, decrease it by 1 (n -= 1), print again — do this for 3, 2, 1, then print «Start!».

Expected output:
3
2
1
«Start!»
tasks.hint: Three pairs of “print, decrease” (the last decrease can be left out) and the final line.

tasks.title: A mutable string
tasks.statement:
Create a mutable string `let mut s = String::from("Hello");`, append the text ", world!" to it with the push_str method, and print: «Hello, world!».

Expected output:
«Hello, world!»
tasks.hint: String::from("…") creates an owned string, and s.push_str("…") appends to the end; this needs mut.

tasks.title: Body mass index
tasks.statement:
weight = 70.0 (kg), height = 1.75 (m). BMI = weight / (height * height). Print «BMI: 22.9».

Expected output:
«BMI: 22.9»
tasks.hint: All the numbers are floats — with a dot; format {:.1}.

tasks.title: Fix it: the type does not fit the value
tasks.statement:
The program does not build: the number 5.5 cannot be stored in a variable of type i32. Fix the type so that the output is «5.5».

Expected output:
5.5
tasks.hint: f64 (or f32) suits fractional numbers.

tasks.title: Fix it: a variable without a value
tasks.statement:
The program reads a variable that may not have been assigned a value. Fix it so that it prints «large» when n = 150, and «small» otherwise.

Expected output:
«large»
tasks.hint: Add an else branch: then the value is assigned on all paths.

tasks.title: Final program: salary
tasks.statement:
Salary = 120000. The tax is 13% — subtract it (use integer arithmetic: salary * 13 / 100). Then shadow salary with the amount after tax and print three lines: «Tax: 15600», «Net pay: 104400» and «Monthly rent: 31320» (30% of what remains, again salary * 30 / 100).

Expected output:
«Tax: 15600
Net pay: 104400
Monthly rent: 31320»
tasks.hint: tax = salary * 13 / 100; then let salary = salary - tax; rent = salary * 30 / 100.
